reason: Every entry below now carries a terminal status and the boundary's production path runs, but two gaps keep the file out of ready-for-audit. commitChecked still names the commit the slice started from, because the evidence applies to the commit that carries this update and no field can name its own SHA; refresh it to the landed head before preparing a pass. And the entries cover this slice's boundary alone, so sourceReview attests to nothing about the goal's remaining slices -- readobjnam() and its chain, hold_another_object() and prinv() -- which need the boundary re-scoped.

boundary.startingEvent: Either dispatch byte: \u0017 (Ctrl-W) reaching rhack(), or the newline closing #wizwish at the extended-command prompt reaching doextcmd().
boundary.endingEvent: The painted top line 'For what do you wish?' and each subsequent keystroke echo, which tty_getlin() renders. The port then fails closed at zap.c:6346, after mungspaces(buf) and before the ESC test, so it consumes and echoes the whole typed line and refuses the submitting Enter.
boundary.validInputs: A wizard-mode game reached through playmode:debug. Both dispatch routes. A non-debug game pressing Ctrl-W, which must print Unavailable command 'wizwish'. The m prefix is inside the boundary by source but outside the port's reach: readSimpleCommand() refuses the reqmenu key itself, which the open deferral 'the m prefix loses a frame' already tracks.
boundary.observables: The prompt text and its cursor, every echoed keystroke, the absence of 'You may wish for an object.', and an unchanged random-number log: no call in scope draws.
boundary.exclusions: zap.c:6346 onward, meaning readobjnam() and everything after it, which is the next slice. zap.c:6334's wish_history_menu() arm, dead because DEBUG is undefined. zap.c:6330's cmdassist suffix, reachable only at tries > 0.

candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: The slice-selector did not read readobjnam_postparse1() (objnam.c:4240-4663) in full, so its claim that only 'amulet of life saving' may need a class-word strip is a lead. That bears on later slices rather than this one. The five makewish() call sites outside wizcmds.c, where 'You may wish for an object.' does print, were read for their flags.verbose state but their own behavior was not traced.

Two tests in scripts/wizard-wish.test.mjs drive the byte through the port instead, one at makewish() and one through the whole command.

sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable within the boundary was traced against nethack-c/upstream/src/: wizcmds.c wiz_wish() whole, zap.c makewish() 6313-6345 statement by statement, cmd.c can_do_extcmd() and rhack()'s dispatch and result handling at 3688-3827, and the extcmdlist row's flags. The trace covered state and random-number order, and found no random-number call inside the boundary; the development score's random-number totals are unchanged for every session but the two the wish unlocks. Stubs, stops and partial implementations were identified: the two dispatch seams now dispatch, js/zap.js holds makewish()'s head, and the arms that cannot occur or belong to a later slice each carry the source condition that settles them. Two limits stand, both recorded above: readobjnam_postparse1() was not read in full, and the five makewish() call sites outside wizcmds.c were read only for their flags.verbose state. The boundary itself is narrower than the goal, so this review says nothing about the goal's remaining slices.
